What MindLeverX is, in one paragraph

MindLeverX is a generative engine optimization practice for mid-market B2B SaaS. It measures whether AI answer engines cite, quote and recommend a brand, publishes every figure with a provenance label, and engineers the content and technical changes that move those measurements.

SOURCE: MINDLEVERX METHODOLOGY V1.0 · JUL 2026
01 · The practice

Small, and specific about it.

MindLeverX is a single-operator practice. There is no team page because there is no team yet. That is a deliberate disclosure rather than an omission: a practice that sells measurement should not begin by asking you to take an unmeasured claim about itself on trust.

The work is narrow on purpose. One category — mid-market B2B SaaS. One methodology, versioned. One question: when a buyer asks an answer engine who solves this problem, does your brand appear in the answer, and can you prove the change when it does?

What that buys you is the thing agencies at scale struggle to offer — a straight line from the person taking the measurement to the person explaining it.

What this practice does
  • Scores a domain against the four dimensions of Methodology V1.0.
  • Monitors answer engines on a fixed, versioned prompt panel, so movement is comparable between runs.
  • Delivers the fix path — recommendations and draft-ready artifacts, not a dashboard alone.
  • Runs human deep-audits across all four dimensions when the automated read isn't enough.
What it does not do
  1. Guarantee outcomes. No promised rankings, citation rates or share of voice. Process guarantees only — the method is fixed, the numbers are what they are.
  2. Publish to your site. Content artifacts are delivered as drafts for your approval. No CMS credentials change hands.
  3. Compare numbers that aren't comparable. Readings of different provenance are never averaged or trended together.
02 · The method

Four dimensions, one composite, versioned.

Methodology V1.0 scores four things and takes their unweighted mean. The version number matters more than the score: a rubric that changes silently makes every trend meaningless. The full definition of GEO is here →

1

Technical access

Whether answer engines can reach, render and parse the pages at all — crawler policy, server rendering, structured data, heading structure.

Crawlable
2

Content quotability

Whether a passage stands alone well enough to be lifted into an answer with no surrounding context — answer-first definitions, dated and sourced claims.

Crawlable
3

Off-site authority

Whether the wider web treats the brand as the entity that belongs in the answer — corroboration across the sources engines actually read.

Off-site
4

Measured visibility

Whether the brand actually appears, run against a fixed prompt panel locked at baseline, so a later reading can be compared with an earlier one.

Panel run
03 · Why provenance

A number without a label is a claim.

Every figure MindLeverX publishes carries a label describing how it was obtained: MEASURED (tool), MEASURED (live), INFERRED (proxy) or NOT MEASURED. The label travels with the number wherever it appears — in a scorecard, a report, an alert or on this site.

The rule that follows from it is the one the whole product rests on: figures of different provenance are never compared. A measured reading and an inferred one do not average into a meaningful score, and a trend built from both describes nothing.

It is also why measurement here is honest about its own limits. Readings are taken through engine APIs against a fixed prompt panel; API answers are a proxy for the consumer products people actually use, which differ in retrieval, personalization and interface. That caveat sits at the foot of every page rather than in a footnote nobody reads.

The practical test of all this is the case study we run on ourselves: the same methodology, the same labels, and NOT MEASURED printed wherever a reading does not exist yet. See our own scorecard →

The four labels
  • MEASURED (tool) — a reading taken by an instrument, with the date and method recorded.
  • MEASURED (live) — observed directly in a live engine response.
  • INFERRED (proxy) — derived from something adjacent, never presented as direct.
  • NOT MEASURED — no reading exists. Published as such, with the condition that would unlock it.
04 · Contact

How to reach the practice.

The free GEO Readiness Audit is the front door. It scores your domain against the methodology above and is the fastest way to start a conversation with something concrete in it — your numbers rather than a sales call.

Direct email is not live yet. The domain is owned; the mailbox is not provisioned. Rather than publish an address that bounces or borrow one from another business, this page says so and will carry the address the day it exists.

Requests that need a person before then — scoping a deep audit, security review, anything a form can't hold — should come through the audit with a note in the domain field; every submission is read by the operator, not a queue.
